one_liner: Senior Executive Service role helping run USDA Farm Service Agency's nationwide network of 51 state and ~2,200 county offices delivering farm and loan programs.
fit_summary: This is an SES executive job requiring demonstrated senior-level leadership of national agricultural programs, including Farm Bill, Farm Loan, and disaster programs, across a large decentralized field organization. Daniel's consulting background at IEM and strong policy knowledge are relevant to disaster programs and stakeholder engagement, but nothing on file shows executive-level supervision of a large dispersed workforce or agricultural program leadership. A QRB certification would also be required before appointment.
eligibility: Open to the public: hiring paths include public, competitive, excepted, and SES, so no federal status is required.
Your two-page resume must demonstrate all five Executive Core Qualifications, and a separate narrative is not accepted.

You must meet the Technical Qualification: senior-level experience leading complex national agricultural programs (Farm Bill, Farm Programs, Farm Loan Programs, disaster and conservation) in a large decentralized field organization.
Unless you are already SES or SESCDP-certified, the OPM Qualifications Review Board must certify you after selection, followed by a one-year probationary period.
strategy: Be realistic: apply only if your IEM role included leading teams, budgets, or national-scale federal disaster or agricultural program delivery. Otherwise, target GS-11/12/13 FSA or FEMA program and outreach roles instead.
If you apply, build the two-page resume around the five ECQs, with one or two quantified bullets each (team size, budget, number of jurisdictions served). Use 11-point font and 0.8-inch margins.
Frame your IEM work around any USDA or FEMA disaster-recovery programs you supported, stating your client, your scope, and your results, without overstating your title or authority.
Use your policy expertise for the 'Commitment to the Rule of Law and Principles of the American Founding' ECQ, with concrete examples of applying statutes or regulations.
Highlight stakeholder work with federal, state, and local agencies and community groups, since this matches both the partnership duty and the TQ.
Submit before the closing date of November 13, 2026, and make sure every hour-per-week and date detail appears briefly on each job entry.
resume_bullets: Led [number]-person team at IEM supporting [federal/state client] disaster recovery program across [number] jurisdictions, managing [budget/contract value] and delivering [specific result].
Interpreted [statute/regulation, e.g., Stafford Act provisions] for [client] officials, producing guidance adopted by [number] offices and reducing [processing time/errors] by [amount].
Built partnerships with [agencies/community organizations] to assess community needs after [event], informing [recommendation] adopted by [client leadership].
interview_questions: Describe a time you led a geographically dispersed team through a major change. How did you hold people accountable?
How would you ensure consistent delivery of Farm Bill programs across 51 state offices and 2,200 county offices?
Give an example of cutting waste or improving efficiency through process or technology changes.
How have you used field feedback to recommend policy changes to senior leadership?
watch_outs: The TQ demands specific agricultural program leadership, so applicants without it will likely be rated ineligible.
SES selection requires OPM QRB certification, which few first-time federal applicants without executive experience pass.
Content past page two will not be read and may lead to disqualification.
The position is based in Washington, DC, which means a commute from Manassas, though telework is available.
